own_solution.law: Snell's law gives theta_r = asin(sin(40 degrees)/1.8) = 20.92 degrees. Side reflections preserve the axial velocity, so t = nL/(c cos(theta_r)). With c = 3.0e8 m/s and L = 2 m, t = 12.8471 ns. An extension q gives t = n(2 + q)/(c cos(theta_r)).
assumptions: Geometrical optics applies to the straight rod.
The nondispersive glass gives pulse speed c/n.
The inline extension provides a continuous path through the same glass.

notes: I withdraw the pass-1 rendering_not_minimal flag: pass 2 explicitly identifies T97AD and TACC7 as numeral-free controls, rather than numerical minimal pairs. Both claimed minimal pairs preserve 1.3 m and change the intended attachment. The relevant extension answers for q = 0.7, 1.3 and 2.2 m are respectively 17.3436, 21.1977 and 26.9789 ns, agreeing with every certified value. All disconnected and diameter variants retain 12.8471 ns. Diameter affects reflection spacing but cancels from transit time; accounting for partial first and last zigzag legs gives the exact path L/cos(theta_r). The earlier-run-only wording excludes the extension from the present run. Unit conversions and stated numerical precision are consistent.
